transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Novum Head of ML), Priya Das (Novum Eng Mgr), Evan Brooks (Novum Security), Zoe Lin (Novum DS)

Summary: quick PLG/self-serve discovery focused on Redwood API quickstart, free credits, and time-to-first-token. High-level qualification: batch vs low-latency use, data sensitivity, timeline for POC.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, quick intro  samir from our se team is here, we'll run through what the quickstart looks like and answer any infra/security q's
00:18 Liam: hey, thanks, i'm liam, we run model infra at novum, mostly evaluating hosted-first approach, curious about how fast we can get going and cost/latency tradeoffs
00:27 Samir: great  quick question up front, is this for a user-facing low-latency feature or more batched inference?
00:34 Priya: it's user-facing; aim for interactive chat and some assist features in our app. Target p95 under 500ms ideally, but we're flexible if costs balloon
00:45 Samir: ok good, that's helpful. Redwood's PLG quickstart typically gets you time-to-first-token in minutes  sign up, free credits, api key, call the hosted endpoint. We'll show an example config  also note dedicated pools if you need consistent p95 latency
01:02 Evan: quick security question  are you SOC 2 certified? how do you handle encryption and KMS? and retention on hosted?
01:12 Maya: yes we are SOC 2 Type II, we can send the attestation. For hosted we encrypt in transit and at rest, customer keys supported via KMS for Dedicated/Private. Retention is configurable; default ephemeral for PLG trials but enterprise plans allow retention policies and export. we'll share the docs after the call
01:32 Zoe: do you have any sample notebooks or playbooks for the quickstart? our data scientists prefer a python notebook flow
01:39 Maya: absolutely  quickstart includes python and curl snippets, sample notebooks for chat, embeddings, and similarity. free credits tie to the account so you can hit production-like requests without card charges for the pilot
01:50 Liam: perfect. on latency  can you explain time-to-first-token more? i've seen disparity between providers, e.g., cold start vs warmed endpoints
02:05 Samir: sure  time-to-first-token depends on model size, request length, and whether the runner has warmed host or if it needs to load weights. For hosted plg endpoints we do warm pools for common model sizes; for unpredictable spikes the startup cost can add 100-300ms for some larger models. Dedicated eliminates that variability by keeping GPUs allocated to your pool
02:26 Priya: is there an autoscale/burst option? we don't want to overcommit but need predictable latency during peak usage
02:33 Samir: yes  Dedicated has reserved baseline capacity plus burst lanes; you configure autoscale policies. For PLG hosted we have a multi-tenant warm strategy and fallbacks to compatible model variants if capacity is constrained
02:50 Liam: ok  what's the typical cost delta between hosted vs dedicated? high level ballpark is fine
02:57 Maya: hosted is usage-based, good for evals and early prod; Dedicated is commit-based monthly pricing but lower per-token unit economics at scale. we'll send a pricing snapshot, but rough: if you're > X tokens/day or need strict p95, Dedicated often makes sense  samir can show math for your expected volume
03:18 Evan: for security, if we go hosted for the pilot, can we ensure logs/audits don't include PII? we may need to filter before sending
03:26 Maya: yes you can pre-filter client-side, we also have routes that obfuscate or drop certain fields. For enterprise we offer VPC/private control plane and HSM integrations. we'll include the security playbook in the follow-up
03:45 Zoe: also curious about reranking and embeddings costs  our workflow uses embeddings for retrieval-heavy stuff, want to understand batching and cache optimizations
03:55 Samir: embeddings are per-call unit pricing; we recommend using automatic prefix caching and batch embeddings for throughput. Redwood Optimize suggests batching sizes and quantization for your workload  the quickstart includes heuristics you can try
04:12 Priya: one practical question  how fast can we get an engineer to a token in our app, like time-to-first-token from sign-up to sample call?
04:22 Maya: usually under 10 minutes: sign up, create api key, run the sample notebook which calls the endpoint and streams first token. we'll provide a checklist. If you want, we can do a screenshare session where we walk through sign-up and a quick call
04:40 Liam: that'd be helpful. for the pilot, i'm thinking a single chat endpoint with our domain-specific prompts and a small set of users  estimate ~5k requests/day to start
04:50 Samir: that's small enough to run on hosted with good cost; we'll simulate latency with similar payloads. also recommend pinning a model version and doing a canary rollout if you decide to change models during pilot
05:03 Evan: curious about data residency  our EU customers' data must stay in eu regions. is that supported on hosted?
05:11 Maya: yes, we support region pinning for hosted accounts and also Dedicated/Private deployments inside EU. for PLG trials region availability varies by signup region but we'll confirm for you
05:25 Priya: any rough onboarding timeline if we later move to Dedicated or Private? we need to plan for procurement
05:32 Maya: Dedicated onboarding is generally a few weeks  depends on capacity and networking (VPC peering). Private on-prem tends to take longer and involves additional security review. For now, hosted pilot keeps procurement light
05:45 Liam: do you have any known gotchas when moving from hosted to dedicated? like model variant compatibilities or tokenization differences
05:53 Samir: models are identical; differences come from quantization profiles and kernel selection. we have a migration checklist; you may see slight latency behavior changes if you switch quantization or instance types. Samir: (laughs) it's not usually an issue, but worth validating in a small canary
06:12 Zoe: about SDKs  we prefer python, any official clients?
06:16 Maya: yes official python and node SDKs with streaming and function-calling support. they'll be in the quickstart repo
06:25 Priya: what about rate limits for the trial? we don't want to be throttled during initial tests
06:31 Maya: trials come with reasonable default quotas; if you hit them we'll bump for pilot. For production you configure per-route limits and quotas in the console
06:42 Liam: are there existing customers in our space? a benchmark or case study would be helpful
06:47 Maya: we have a case study with a similar analytics SaaS  i'll link it. also Samir can share performance numbers for comparable workloads
06:55 Samir: i'll prepare a short benchmark doc with p50/p95 for typical chat workloads and an example config for your payload sizes
07:05 Evan: final clarifying Q on KMS  if we want customer-managed keys on hosted, is that available or only for Dedicated/Private?
07:12 Maya: customer-managed keys are generally supported on Dedicated and Private; hosted trials use our managed keys but we can discuss enterprise options and transitional arrangements
07:25 Priya: timeline  we're evaluating over the next 3 weeks, technical POC in two weeks if quickstart looks good. procurement gate in ~6 weeks possibly for Dedicated
07:36 Maya: sounds good  next steps i'll send the quickstart link + free credits, samir will send a bench config, and evan you'll get SOC 2 + security docs. let's schedule a 30-min screenshare quickstart walkthrough early next week
07:52 Liam: thanks folks, that's helpful
07:56 Maya: cool, we'll follow up with the notes and links
